title: Non-blocking findings from PR #319's review (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups)
description: Non-blocking findings recorded by pr-reviewer's code-review/verify-elder-signal passes on PR #319, tracked here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators's same-calendar-day response cache (app.api.indicator_history_cache.IndicatorHistoryResponseCache) can serve a stale `trading_mode` field after the global trading mode changes between requests within the same calendar day: a cached IndicatorHistoryResponse's `trading_mode` is baked in at write time (app/api/routers/stocks.py's `cached_response = response_cache.get(ticker, range)` check returns the stored response as-is on a hit) and never refreshed to the freshly-resolved current setting. Narrow in practice -- only reachable while the swing branch is still being taken with a cache hit (e.g. day_trader mode configured with no triple yet, which is treated the same as swing), not once a fully-intraday triple is active (that always bypasses the cache entirely) -- but undocumented as an accepted tradeoff the way this same cache's OHLCV/signal staleness already is (see IndicatorHistoryResponse.points's own field description). Worth either invalidating/excluding this field from the cached payload and re-attaching the freshly-resolved trading_mode_setting_out on every cache hit, or explicitly documenting this as an accepted staleness case alongside the existing one.

GET /api/portfolio/risk's first-pass loop (app/api/routers/portfolio.py's get_risk, the loop populating stops/weekly_by_id/daily_by_id) duplicates ~15 lines of near-identical logic (drop_malformed_daily_bars, the len<2 check, the protective_stop try/except ValueError) across the day_trader_active and swing branches, differing only in where daily_ohlcv/weekly_ohlcv come from (day-trader legs already fetched concurrently up front vs. a per-position swing weekly fetch). A future fix to that shared sequence (a new guard, a different exception type) has to be applied in both places by hand -- worth factoring the shared drop_malformed_daily_bars/length-check/protective_stop steps into one helper taking (daily_ohlcv_raw, weekly_ohlcv) once each branch has resolved those two inputs its own way.

app.portfolio.risk.position_risk_pct's 'distance to stop' computation in day-trader mode mixes a swing-derived `current_price` (this ticker's ordinary EOD daily-chart close, per PortfolioResponse.trading_mode's own field description) with a day-trader-mode-derived `protective_stop` (computed from the active triple's IBKR-fetched intermediate leg) for the same position -- the resulting 2%-rule risk percentage spans two different data sources/timeframes for the same ticker rather than one live intraday price against a live intraday stop. This follows the already-reviewed backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk (PR #317) generalization precedent, not something introduced fresh by PR #319, but PR #319 is what makes it reachable end-to-end via the real GET /api/portfolio/risk endpoint with a real per-position IBKR fetch, and no `decisions` entry anywhere in this feature's chain addresses this specific current_price/stop timeframe mismatch. Worth deciding (and recording via `decisions`) whether this is an accepted tradeoff (matching current_price/equity's own already-documented 'always swing-derived regardless of mode' precedent) or worth a dedicated live-intraday-price fetch for this specific calculation in day-trader mode.

backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_get.py's TestDayTraderMode class only exercises single-position scenarios (one PositionORM per test). The discriminating 'does the concurrent fan-out mix up which ticker gets which outcome' test exists at the unit level (tests/unit/api/test_day_trader_signal.py's test_maps_each_distinct_ticker_to_its_own_outcome_not_a_shared_or_swapped_one) but not as a GET /api/portfolio integration test with 2+ held positions of genuinely different tickers/outcomes -- worth adding one so a regression in how compute_day_trader_signals_concurrently's results get matched back to the right position in get_portfolio's own loop would be caught at the router-integration level too, not only at the day_trader_signal.py unit level.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 1 (stale cached trading_mode) is FIXED, not just documented: on a cache hit, get_indicator_history now returns `cached_response.model_copy(update={"trading_mode": trading_mode_setting_out})` -- re-attaching the freshly-resolved current setting to every cache hit -- rather than serving the stored payload's own baked-in field as-is.
decisions.rationale: Unlike the cache's existing, accepted OHLCV/signal staleness (a real recompute the cache deliberately skips to save the provider round-trip), `trading_mode` isn't part of the cache key and costs nothing to refresh: `trading_mode_setting_out` is already resolved once per request before the cache is even consulted, so overwriting one field on the cached model via `model_copy(update=...)` is a cheap, correct fix with no schema/migration/invalidation-policy work, unlike the alternative of excluding the field from the cached JSON entirely (which would need a schema version bump or a nullable-then-backfilled column). Verified via a new discriminating integration test (test_cache_hit_still_echoes_a_trading_mode_change_made_after_it_was_cached, tests/integration/test_stocks_indicator_history_cache.py) that mutation-tests the fix itself: reverting the model_copy call to `return cached_response` makes the test fail with the stale 'swing' value instead of the freshly-set 'day_trader' one, confirming the test genuinely discriminates.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 2 (get_risk's ~15-line duplicated drop_malformed_daily_bars/length-check/protective_stop sequence) is factored into a new module-level helper, `_stop_and_filtered_daily(position, daily_ohlcv_raw) -> tuple[float, pd.DataFrame] | None`, called from both the day_trader_active and swing branches of the first-pass loop -- each branch still resolves its own `daily_ohlcv_raw`/`weekly_ohlcv` its own way (day-trader legs already fetched concurrently vs. a per-position swing weekly fetch) and still owns its own weekly-side error handling, but the shared filter/length-check/protective_stop-try-except sequence now lives in exactly one place.
decisions.rationale: The two branches' shared sequence was byte-for-byte identical (same drop_malformed_daily_bars call, same `len(daily_ohlcv) < 2` guard, same protective_stop try/except ValueError) -- a textbook extract-function refactor with no behavior change, verified by the existing GET /api/portfolio/risk test suite (all passing unchanged, plus mypy clean) since this is a pure internal reshuffle of already-tested logic, not new logic needing new tests. Kept as a private helper on portfolio.py itself (not moved into app.portfolio.risk) since it's specific to this router's own first-pass-loop shape (returns a tuple the caller immediately destructures into stops/daily_by_id, not a general-purpose domain function).

decisions.decision: Checklist item 3 (position_risk_pct mixing a swing-derived current_price with a day-trader-derived protective_stop for the same position) is left AS-IS -- explicitly accepted as a documented tradeoff, not fixed with a dedicated live-intraday-price fetch. Documented in two places: app.portfolio.risk.position_risk_pct's own docstring (a new paragraph naming the mismatch explicitly and pointing at this decision) and RiskPosition.position_risk_pct's field description in app/api/schemas.py (so it's visible in the OpenAPI contract itself, not just internal code).
decisions.rationale: This matches current_price/equity's own already-documented 'always swing-derived regardless of trading mode' precedent (PortfolioResponse.trading_mode's field description, RiskResponse.trading_mode's field description) -- position_risk_pct's current_price input is exactly the same always-swing-derived value those fields already commit to, so treating protective_stop's own mode-dependence as the one exception needing a bespoke live-intraday fetch would be inconsistent with that existing precedent, not a fix to it. A dedicated live-intraday-price fetch for this one calculation would also need its own error-handling/degrade-gracefully contract (what happens when that fetch fails but current_price/protective_stop are both otherwise available?), a second concurrent-fetch pipeline alongside the existing per-ticker leg fan-out, and a decision about whether GET /api/portfolio's own current_price should then diverge from GET /api/portfolio/risk's -- real, separable scope this follow-up task's own checklist wording ('worth deciding... or worth a dedicated fetch') treats as optional, not mandatory. PR #317/#319's own reviewers already treated the underlying current_price/protective_stop mode split as an accepted, reviewed tradeoff (PR #319's pr-decision notes: 'confirmed via e.position.current_price's always-swing-derived contract at portfolio.py:358... correctly non-blocking, not a bug') -- this decision doesn't reopen that, it just gives it its own explicit, findable `decisions` record and doc text, which is what the finding itself said was actually missing ('no decisions entry anywhere in this feature's chain addresses this specific... mismatch').

decisions.decision: Checklist item 4's multi-position discriminating test is added as test_two_distinct_tickers_each_get_their_own_signal_not_a_shared_or_swapped_one in tests/integration/test_portfolio_get.py's TestDayTraderMode -- two held positions (AAPL, MSFT), with AAPL given a fully resolvable/BUY-shaped IBKR bar set and MSFT deliberately given an unresolvable conid (via a new `_PerTickerStubIBKRProvider`, since the existing `_StubIBKRProvider` shares one fixed bar set across every ticker in a request and so can't itself produce two genuinely different per-ticker outcomes) -- asserting AAPL ends up with a real BUY signal and MSFT ends up with a null signal/confidence/confidence_band, keyed correctly to each position's own ticker.
decisions.rationale: A same-outcome-for-both fixture (e.g. both BUY, or both unavailable) wouldn't actually discriminate a ticker-swap bug -- the test would pass even if compute_day_trader_signals_concurrently's results got matched to the wrong position, since both positions would show the same thing either way. Two genuinely different outcomes (a resolved signal vs. an unresolvable one) makes a swap visible. Verified this test itself actually discriminates (not just happy-path) via mutation testing: temporarily changed `_fan_out_per_ticker` (app/api/day_trader_signal.py) to return the last-completed future's result for every ticker key (the same mutation PR #319's own review already used to validate the underlying unit test) and confirmed this new integration test fails (AAPL's signal came back null instead of BUY) while the file's existing single-position tests kept passing -- meaning only this new multi-position test actually catches that class of bug at the router-integration level; the mutation was then reverted (git diff on app/api/day_trader_signal.py is clean, confirming no production code needed to change for this item).
